newsitem.title: POLAND: Ameritech might sell Centertel stake.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech might sell Centertel stake.

text.p: Ameritech Corp, owner of a stake in mobile phone operator Centertel SA, is considering selling its stake to the firm's other two owners, a source close to Ameritech said on Wednesday.

"Negotiations are still going and all parties are trying to figure out what to do with the situation within Centertel...but no agreement between the parties has been reached at the moment," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters on Wednesday.
On Tuesday the Polish daily Gazeta Wyborcza reported that Ameritech wanted to sell its 24.5-percent stake in Centertel to telecom monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) and France Telecom.
It said that after the deal TPSA and France Telecom, which now hold 51 percent and 24.5 percent of the Centertel joint venture respectively, would have 65 percent and 35 percent.
The daily, which cited unofficial sources, said the sale could be completed by the end of the month for $50 million but would be subject to approval by Poland's anti-monopoly authority.
The paper said the move would allow Ameritech to concentrate on operations in Hungary, and that the U.S.-based firm had become weary of disagreements with TPSA.

The partnership in the venture turned sour last year when TPSA, arguing its role in the company did not reflect its majority shareholding, began seeking more say in Centertel's management and a bigger share in the company's profits.
Earlier this year TPSA blocked Ameritech and France Telecom's plans to seek for Centertel one of two government licences to use a modern digital GSM system.
The licences went to two consortia of Polish and foreign companies, which have launched operations to challenge the position of Centertel, operating an older analogue system.

Ameritech and France Telecom have started international arbitration proceedings against Poland's government, saying that back in 1991 they were promised a GSM licence, while the government argues the promise was not legally binding.
Gazeta Wyborcza reported that the two firms would probably withdraw from the proceedings if the sale went ahead.
